3481177_d6c3a647.text: One of the well-defined sexually dimorphic structures in the brain is the sexually dimorphic nucleus, a cluster of cells located in the preoptic area of the hypothalamus. The rodent sexually dimorphic nucleus of the preoptic area can be delineated histologically using conventional Nissl staining or immunohistochemically using calbindin D28K immunoreactivity
3481177_d6c3a647.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

3481177_1098a86b.text: The sexually dimorphic nucleus has been specifically defined in the brains of human and other mammalian and non-mammalian and includes the third interstitial nucleus of the anterior hypothalamus in humans (Allen et al., 1989)(Allen et al., 1990) , the ovine sexually dimorphic nucleus in the medial preoptic area (Roselli et al., 2004) , the medial preoptic and anterior hypothalamic regions in rhesus monkeys (Byne, 1998) , a specific area in the medial preoptic nucleus in quail (Viglietti‐Panzica et al., 1986) , and the sexually dimorphic nucleus of the preoptic area in rats (Gorski et al., 1978)(Gorski et al., 1980) . The human sexually dimorphic nucleus of the preoptic area is located in the medial part of the preoptic area, between the dorsolateral supraoptic nucleus and the rostral pole of the paraventricular nucleus (Hofman et al., 1989)
3481177_1098a86b.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

3481177_9891c854.text: As demonstrated in laboratory animal studies, the sexually dimorphic nucleus is critically implicated in sexual behavior (Arendash et al., 1983)(Rayen et al., 2013)
3481177_9891c854.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

3481177_562d502e.text: the sexually dimorphic nucleus of the preoptic area are positive for tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), yet many TH-positive axonand synapse-like structures are found there
3481177_562d502e.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

3481177_17d4bd9d.text: The sexually dimorphic nucleus of the preoptic area is highlighted by calbindin-D28K immunoreactivity: no TH-positive cells were found, but fine axon-like projections/synaptic structures were seen
3481177_17d4bd9d.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

3481177_1dd3b718.text: the anteroventral periventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (AVPV) consists mainly of TH-positive neurons
3481177_1dd3b718.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

3481177_17c756ed.text: Neural stem cell activity has been identified in the hypothalamus (Dahiya et al., 2011)(Ahmed et al., 2008)(Kokoeva et al., 2005) (Kokoeva et al., 2007)(Pérez-Martín et al., 2010) , a territory which includes the sexually dimorphic nucleus of the preoptic area. Neural progenitor cells from the ependymal layer of the 3 rd ventricle migrate and differentiate into neurons in the hypothalamus (Ernst et al., 2005)(Xu et al., 2005)(Park et al., 1996)
3481177_17c756ed.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures
